newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher after storage data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher after storage data.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly higher Thursday ahead of the holiday weekend as a lower-than-expected AGA number lifted August on ACCESS, market sources said.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 76 bcf, well-below average estimates at 85-95 bcf.
On ACCESS, August last traded 1.5 cents higher at $2.082.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.075 to $2.08 after settling to the downside Wednesday at $2.067 per mmBtu.
NYMEX will close for the Independence Day holiday at 1300 EDT Thursday.

Overall stocks were still 216 bcf, or 16 percent, over year-ago levels. Eastern storage gained 56 bcf and was 11 percent above last year, while producing region inventories remained 52 percent over 1996 levels. Western stocks continued to lag year-ago levels by nine percent.
Technically, traders said August support was at $2.055 and $2. Resistance was seen at $2.12, $2.15 and then along the down trendline at $2.27.

In Wednesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped a few cents to about $2.10. Midcon pipes were down slightly at $2.02-2.03. New York city gate gas was quoted three to four cents lower in the high-$2.30s.
